description: A game-development meetup where people exchange skills, discuss their projects and find collaborators.

participants.name: Artist, writer and designer
participants.offers: I make art, write and design game concepts and systems. I have been doing these things casually for a while, without professional experience. I already have some planned game ideas and concepts written down. Programming has been the biggest obstacle when I have tried making games myself. I am new to using online platforms to communicate.
participants.needs: I want to make games for fun and gain experience, in any style or genre. I am looking for a person or small team with programming skills; experience level is not important if they can make simple functional games. We could implement and test my ideas, or I could make art for someone else’s project. Please be patient with my limited experience communicating online.

participants.name: GameMaker and JavaScript programmer
participants.offers: I have made a few small games and participated in game jams, mainly using GameMaker. I have also made small multiplayer web projects in JavaScript. I have a couple of small projects paused because I do not want to handle the art myself. I enjoy discussing a game with someone and finding ways to improve its design.
participants.needs: I am looking for an art partner to exchange ideas and design games together. I treat this as a serious hobby, spending a couple of hours a day on average, and would like a partner with a similar commitment. I want to start with very small projects or game jams and polish them before attempting a longer project. We could resume an existing project or start fresh.

participants.name: Artist developing a 2D platformer
participants.offers: I am a casual artist and aspiring game developer. I have been working on a 2D platformer and have a working player controller and tileset. My programming skills are limited, so implementation takes me a long time. The game draws on Mario, Donkey Kong Country and Hollow Knight: exploring an abandoned city after the fall of civilisation and fighting the remaining automatons.
participants.needs: I want a dedicated programmer to help with my programming limitations, speed up progress and contribute to what the game could become. This is an unpaid hobby project with no guaranteed profit if it is released. I want someone tolerant and reasonable who does not rely on AI for coding. My time zone is CDT.

participants.name: Godot programmer for short projects
participants.offers: I am an experienced programmer who has made 2D Godot games for over a year as a hobby, mainly for short game jams. I enjoy implementing interesting mechanics, especially non-platforming puzzles and arcade-style minigames. I am open to trying something new.
participants.needs: I would like to join an upcoming game jam or help with a project that has a clear vision and tight scope. My ideal project can be finished in two or three weeks. I do not want a months-long project with a huge scope, because I want the hobby to stay enjoyable rather than become a second job. I can contribute programming.

participants.name: Godot C# developer and test engineer
participants.offers: I have developed mostly 2D games as a hobby for two years. I now mainly use C# with Godot and also know Unity. I have worked in full-stack development and test automation, and briefly at a small video-game startup. During my computer-science master’s I studied game design and game AI, including state machines and pathfinding.
participants.needs: I am looking for a team for a game jam or a small-to-medium hobby project. Revenue sharing is acceptable, but I would like to work on something small before committing to a larger project. My priority is enjoying the work and improving my skills, rather than making a commercial game for profit.

participants.name: Beginner pixel animator and low-poly modeller
participants.offers: I started pixel art, animation and low-poly 3D modelling a few months ago. I am a beginner and want to contribute while practising, improving and building a portfolio.
participants.needs: I would like a short, manageable, beginner-friendly project with little pressure. I hope to meet a programmer at a similar stage, or a small team with room for an artist. I am open to an existing project or brainstorming something new. I want us to finish something we can both feel proud of, without a large commitment.

participants.name: Unreal programmer seeking artists
participants.offers: I have worked with Unreal Engine for about seven months and can handle programming fairly well. As my projects grow, I struggle to finish them alone. My modelling experience is minimal; creating assets and environments, rigging and animation are my biggest difficulties.
participants.needs: I want to connect with artists or modellers and build a small community where we can make games, improve our skills and learn from each other. Beginners are welcome. I would eventually like a small indie studio, and I also welcome writers, composers, designers and others interested in learning game development.

participants.name: 2D artist learning low-poly 3D
participants.offers: I have around six years of 2D-art experience, including concepts and illustration. I do not do 2D animation and would like to avoid it. I am learning low-poly 3D modelling and still working out rigging. I have a few months of experience with GDScript and Unreal Blueprints, including basic combat, attributes and experience systems. I have finished small game-jam-type projects but have not released a game. My time zone is UTC+3.
participants.needs: I want a programmer to make small 3D single-player games involving building and combat, particularly RTS-like games. I prefer Godot but the engine is flexible, and coding experience matters less than willingness to improve. I would like to try a very small game in about seven days to see how we work together. I value responsive communication and do not want AI-generated art. I hope smaller projects could support longer dream projects; if they eventually earn money, I would favour a 50/50 split.

participants.name: Hobby writer and poet
participants.offers: I am a hobby writer and poet, with no professional creative-writing experience. I would like to try macro-scale world-building, limited-perspective story narratives, NPC dialogue chains, or present full game ideas to a team starting from scratch. My interests include science fiction, fantasy, and darker introspective themes. I am open to trying romance or comedy, though I may not be the best fit for those projects.
participants.needs: I am looking for a game-development team to collaborate with on writing. I offer writing for exposure and credit. I am interested in writing for an existing project or presenting an idea if a team is starting from scratch.

participants.name: 3D modeller and writer
participants.offers: I have experience in 3D modelling and writing, plus some artistic ability. I have some experience with Unreal Engine and a little with Godot; I mainly use Blender and also use CAD. My preferred art style is lower-poly. I am willing to put considerable time and effort into a project, though my availability varies during parts of the year.
participants.needs: I want to make a 3D game as an equal collaboration, with both partners having an equal say and developing the idea together. I am open to ideas and would prefer to start with small games to refine our skills, without aiming for profit or payment until we have a good workflow and quality product. I would like to begin with a simple infinite-runner or tower-defence game, with a few basic models, characters and animations, and a small scope.

participants.name: Pianist and hobby game composer
participants.offers: I am an aspiring game composer and pianist with experience in piano and classical-inspired music. I can also compose in other genres when I can find an approach that fits.
participants.needs: I am offering free music for a video-game project to gain experience. I would prefer a relatively small project rather than a large open-world game. I cannot promise quick turnaround because I do this as a hobby. I need information about the project and the kind of music it needs.

participants.name: Hobby composer and pianist
participants.offers: I am a hobby composer and pianist, most adept at composition, and can also do mixing and sound design. My musical inspirations include Nintendo, Toby Fox, and John Williams. I have worked on smaller projects, including an upcoming game.
participants.needs: I am looking for video-game projects. I would especially like to work with a committed team that has a clear vision, preferably on a larger project, though I am open to hearing about other projects. For commercial projects, payment or revenue share would be welcome and terms are negotiable; for an exciting idea, I am also willing to work for free.

participants.name: Professional writer and editor seeking hobby collaboration
participants.offers: I am a professional writer and editor. I manage writers and edit their work, with a current focus on narrative structure, quotations, and dialogue. I have not worked in game development or game design.
participants.needs: I would like to collaborate with an independent or aspiring game developer on characters, narrative structure, or dialogue as a hobby, not as a career. I would work for free and would value writing credit if the work is released. I would also like to learn about game development and the technical constraints on storytelling. I am open to collaborating with co-writers on games or television and film scripts.

participants.name: Experienced programmer with pixel-art skills
participants.offers: I have more than 12 years of game-making experience and have worked in software development for seven years. My usual game-development tools are Java with libGDX or JavaScript with p5.js. I usually make 2D or 2.5D games and have some 3D experience. I am competent at pixel art, though I would prefer not to make art my main role. I can likely dedicate a couple of hours a day while working full time.
participants.needs: I am looking for an artist and/or game designer to join a small hobby team of two or three people. There is no project idea yet; I would like to brainstorm and make something quick, around game-jam size, to see how we work together. Beginners are welcome.

participants.name: Godot programmer seeking a hobby partner
participants.offers: I have worked on game development on the side for about two years and joined multiple game jams, though I have left personal projects unfinished. I mainly use Godot with GDScript. I work full time as a software engineer. I am interested in a range of game types, especially crafty building and simulation games, roguelike deck builders and multiplayer strategy games, while remaining open to other ideas.
participants.needs: I am looking for a fellow programmer to partner with on hobby game development. I hope to make games as a small two-person team, with the project chosen by agreement. I would like to make games in building, simulation or strategy-oriented genres, but I am open to an interesting idea.

participants.name: Godot programmer and game generalist
participants.offers: I have used Godot for about a year and made a couple of solo Godot projects. I have also recreated classic games such as Pac-Man, Animal Crossing and Space Invaders in other tools, including Python and Unity. I primarily offer programming, with some 2D art, animation and sound effects or music. Most of my experience is in 2D; I have little 3D modelling experience but am open to learning. I have a 2D grid-combat roguelike with basic combat and level progression in progress.
participants.needs: I am looking for a team or partner to make games, gain experience and produce a game I can feel proud of. I would like a project with a memorable story or lesson and a challenge that helps me improve. I can contribute my available free time, with more time if a project strongly interests me. My current project could use help with its story, non-player characters and direction; I am also interested in other collaborations. I cannot promise compensation, though revenue sharing could be considered if I decide to sell my game.

participants.name: MonoGame programmer with an audio-engineering background
participants.offers: I have experimented with MonoGame/XNA for a couple of years and have taken it seriously as a hobby for roughly the past six to twelve months. I have made gameplay prototypes in Unity and Godot. I also have an audio-engineering background.
participants.needs: I am looking for a team or partner for an upcoming game jam or a small project. For a small project, I can commit around two to three hours a day on three or four days each week; for a jam, I could take time off work and devote much more time. An artist would complement my skills, as pixel art is a weakness. I would like to talk with people in a similar position.

participants.name: Godot programmer and hobby artist
participants.offers: I am a software engineer who also enjoys art as a hobby. I am a beginner at game development and have solo-developed a few game-jam projects. I use Godot and am familiar with Blender, Krita and GitHub. I am interested in 3D games and dark, satirical or fantasy themes, but am open to other kinds of games. I can share coding knowledge and learn with collaborators.
participants.needs: I want to join more game jams and start with very small, simple games so potential teammates and I could see how we work together. I am seeking people of any skill level who are willing to learn and grow as a team, with the longer-term hope of making larger games.

participants.name: Unreal programmer seeking a game concept
participants.offers: I recently finished a long-term solo project: a multiplayer first-person shooter made in Unreal Engine. I have over ten years of software-development experience. I offer help with game logic, AI, and single-player or multiplayer implementation. I have a full-time job, so I cannot work every day; Unreal is my strongest engine, though I am interested in learning Godot.
participants.needs: I am looking to join a small hobby project with a level designer or artist who has an intermediate skill level and a clear idea with distinctive selling points. I need to like the game concept enough to stay motivated, and I do not want to make mobile games. I am not interested in learning Unity.

participants.name: Beginner Godot developer seeking collaborators
participants.offers: I have been doing game-development work for a few months and am learning programming, pixel art and sound design. I have finished a small HTML web game and am working on a metroidvania-like game about a robot vampire that can transform into a drone. I work from home and have a lot of time to collaborate. I am based in the UK and am comfortable working across time zones.
participants.needs: I am looking for other people who want to learn, make games and have fun together. I am willing to work with people at any skill level and would like collaborators to bounce ideas off, since working alone can leave me stuck. I am mainly using Godot.

participants.name: Top-down RPG developer seeking an artist
participants.offers: I am developing a top-down RPG and can offer payment for game art, with the scope and price to be agreed according to the amount of work and its quality. I would prefer pixel art, although I am open to other styles. The initial goal is a visually appealing proof of concept.
participants.needs: I am looking for 2D character sprite sheets suitable for skeletal animation, plus tilesets and props. I would like to discuss a paid arrangement; I have also considered revenue share, but the project is still too early for me to make a strong case for that option.

participants.name: 3D prop and environment artist offering game testing
participants.offers: I am a 3D artist who has created props and scenes for university projects and has worked in teams on several projects. I can contribute 3D art and test a game by trying to find bugs and edge cases that a typical play-through might miss.
participants.needs: I am looking for a game project where I can gain practical experience and build my portfolio. I am happy to join an existing project or work with a team to develop a game from an idea. I am offering my contribution for free and can start soon.

participants.name: Hobby game team seeking an artist or animator
participants.offers: I am part of a hobby team that has already completed a week-long game jam and wants to build towards a possible Steam release. The team has three developers, a sound designer and a writer, with a Discord server, project notes and code repository in place. We work at a relaxed pace alongside other jobs and value communication, learning and steady collaboration.
participants.needs: I am looking for an artist, modeller or animator to join our side project. Some professional or hobby experience would help, but we are learning as we go and do not expect immediate commercial success. I am hoping to add someone confident enough to work independently and enjoy taking time to make something good.

participants.name: Medieval tower-defence hobby developer seeking audio help
participants.offers: I am making a medieval-fantasy tower-defence game as a hobby project. It includes towers that can take damage, enemy types that can attack them, tower upgrades and environmental events that affect play. I aim to keep collaboration respectful and relaxed, and I will give full credit when the game is released.
participants.needs: I am looking for a sound designer to create effects for towers, enemies and special abilities, as well as background music that suits the medieval-fantasy setting. I would also welcome creative input on how to improve the game's audio. The role is unpaid.

participants.name: Ren’Py visual-novel hobby developer
participants.offers: I am handling the programming for a Ren’Py visual novel. This is a passion project with no strict deadlines; we can work at our own pace and adapt to each person's available time. Beginners and experienced collaborators are welcome.
participants.needs: I am looking for collaborators in art, writing and sound. I need character designs, backgrounds and other visual assets; story development, dialogue and engaging narrative, with branching-story experience as a plus; and music, sound effects and audio mixing. A consistent visual style and a good ear for atmosphere would help.

participants.name: Sound designer, composer and audio programmer
participants.offers: I am a sound designer, composer, music producer and audio programmer. Over the past two years I have produced beats, composed for friends' projects and collaborated with singers. I can create sound effects, interface sounds, ambiences, transitions and stingers; compose music in a range of genres, including experimental styles; mix and master; and help with audio integration. I use Logic, FL Studio and Ableton Live and have a programming and game-development background.
participants.needs: I am looking to collaborate with beginner-friendly game teams and build experience in game audio. I would like to take on a project's full audio pipeline if that fits, but I can also tailor my contribution to the team's needs.

participants.name: Freelance composer for games and film
participants.offers: I am a freelance composer with several years of experience writing music for films and games. I hold bachelor's and master's degrees from the Royal Birmingham Conservatoire and can compose music to support a project's story and atmosphere, whether it is a platformer, an epic RPG or another kind of game. I am open to working with solo developers and larger teams.
participants.needs: I am looking for new projects and prefer paid work. I understand that small teams and hobby projects may have limited budgets, so I am open to discussing an arrangement that works for both sides.

participants.name: Hobby writer and game-idea creator
participants.offers: I have spent several years writing stories and game ideas. I have a large collection of story concepts and am keen to contribute creative ideas and writing to a game. I am a hobbyist and would like to learn how game development works through collaboration.
participants.needs: I am looking to join a team or an existing project that needs stories and ideas. I do not have practical experience with game engines, art or animation, so I need collaborators who can help bring the writing to life. I am hesitant to share full concepts before finding a team I trust.

participants.name: Isometric city-builder developer seeking a 2D artist
participants.offers: I am developing a personal, passion-led city-builder called We Who Build. Players shape a settlement that changes in response to their architecture and planning choices. I am handling the programming and have made placeholder pixel art. This is an unfunded hobby project with no current commercial goal; I would like to finish and publish a polished game, and I estimate development at around 10–12 months while remaining flexible.
participants.needs: I am looking for a 2D artist to collaborate on isometric art. Hand-drawn and pixel-art approaches are both welcome, provided the work suits the isometric format and gives the game a coherent visual identity.

participants.name: GameMaker developer and designer seeking an artist
participants.offers: I am a hobby game developer and game designer with about five years of experience. I have made several prototypes, including an online top-down fighting-game engine with rollback networking, a Rivals of Aether Workshop character for which I handled design and coding, and a keyboard-controlled platformer engine. I am comfortable with gameplay systems and logic, and my professional full-stack background covers data, back-end and server systems.
participants.needs: I am looking for a serious, long-term collaboration, either to revive my paused mobile gacha shooter or to start a new project. I would especially value an artist, as high-quality asset creation is not my strength and I prefer to focus on design and programming. My speciality is GameMaker, which makes a 2D artist a particularly good fit, though I can learn another engine if the project calls for it.

participants.name: Multi-engine hobby programmer
participants.offers: I have time outside work to contribute as the programmer on a small game. I have used GameMaker, Godot, MonoGame and Love2D, and released a text-mode art editor. I especially enjoy old-school pixel-art games.
participants.needs: I want to work with one or two people on a simple, fun game that can be made casually. I am happy for a partner to focus on art, music or design, and would welcome someone who can help shape the idea.

participants.name: Senior software engineer and Unity programmer
participants.offers: I am a senior software engineer with about four years of C# experience, a master's degree focused on AI, and several hundred hours using Unity. I have also used Blender and can contribute programming to a small game.
participants.needs: I would like to join or form a friendly team making an innovative game with realistic but interesting mechanics. I would value working with another experienced programmer and people with complementary skills. I can contribute a couple of hours a day and weekends around my full-time job. Unity is my preference, though I am learning Unreal Engine 5.

participants.name: Unity C# gameplay programmer
participants.offers: I have seven years of Unity experience and can work in Unity 2D or 3D and C#. My game-development skills include turn-based combat, NPC dialogue, user interfaces, and first- and third-person movement and camera controls. I have worked on two games, including rebuilding a beat-'em-up side-scroller from scratch.
participants.needs: I am seeking paid work with a game team. I have worked on PC games and am open to learning new skills and adapting to a project.

participants.name: Java programmer seeking game-development experience
participants.offers: I know Java beyond the basics and studied programming at school. I can contribute primarily as a programmer, with some additional skills outside programming if useful.
participants.needs: I am looking for a team to make a game and learn through the experience. I do not have a finished game to show yet. I am open to discussing the working arrangement privately.

participants.name: Computer science student and aspiring game programmer
participants.offers: I am studying for a computer science bachelor's degree and have used Unity and Godot, with some experience in C, C++, Python and other languages. I can contribute around 20 hours a week, though this can vary for short periods.
participants.needs: I am looking for a team to make realistic games together while learning and having fun. I am open to different genres and learning new tools. I have taken part in programming competitions but do not yet have a game portfolio.

participants.name: Junior Unity and Unreal game programmer
participants.offers: I am a game programmer starting out, with some game-making experience over the past four or five years. I have worked in 2D and 3D with Unity and in 3D with Unreal, and have recently focused more on Unity 2D. I am open to changing engines to suit a project's ideas.
participants.needs: I want to make small but meaningful games with a couple of collaborators, or join a team of about two or three people and no more than four or five. Projects could last from one or two weeks up to three months, with game jams as a way to keep scope tight. I would ideally work with a designer and an artist, though I am flexible. Teammates should be able to share and receive constructive criticism, and contribute a little each day, around 30 minutes to an hour. I want to build portfolio pieces and experience.

participants.name: Unity prototyper seeking a game designer
participants.offers: I have used Unity for a few years, collected assets and made prototypes. I also do some creative writing and can help build a playable 3D project, including with simple purchased assets.
participants.needs: I am looking for someone with game-design skills to collaborate on very small projects, such as a single-scene experiment or game-jam entry. My main aim is to learn by doing; perhaps we could try a larger project later. I am interested in adventure games, shooters, racing, children's and educational games, and story-driven games.

participants.name: Experienced RPG programmer
participants.offers: I have years of game-programming experience and have worked on both 2D and 3D RPGs. My current schedule makes 2D metroidvanias especially appealing, though I am open to other genres.
participants.needs: I want to join a team that is committed to finishing a polished game. Past teams have abandoned projects or lacked commitment, so seeing a project through to completion matters to me.

participants.name: Programmer with a 3D platformer concept
participants.offers: I am an experienced programmer and have written a game design document for my own game concept. The project is a 3D platformer with themed worlds and distinct mechanics for each world.
participants.needs: I need a game designer to help make the concept, levels and world design more distinctive. I have limited skills in sprites, 3D modelling and audio, and would eventually like a dedicated sound artist. My budget is limited, so I am open to students, aspiring professionals building a portfolio, or experienced people interested in earning extra income; revenue share or direct payment may be discussed.

participants.name: Artist and designer with a fighting-game concept
participants.offers: I am an artist and designer trying to get into game development, and I have some art for a small fighting-game concept. I have the most experience with Unity and GameMaker.
participants.needs: I am looking for a programmer to help make a two-player mind-game fighter. Players choose characters and stages, then guess an opponent's directional choice; three correct guesses win a round, while a miss resets the combo and gives the opponent a turn. Characters would have one-use abilities such as changing a choice mid-attack, adding extra directions, blocking, doubling combo progress or revealing the opponent's choice. I want to develop more ability ideas with a collaborator.
